passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel cognitive enhancer on reaction time in healthy adults. A double‑blind, placebo‑controlled design was used with 120 participants randomly assigned to one of four groups: placebo (Control), 5 mg (Low Dose), 10 mg (Medium Dose), and 20 mg (High Dose). After a 30‑minute absorption period, participants completed a computerized simple reaction time task. Mean reaction times (RT) and standard deviations (SD) were recorded for each group. The study aimed to determine whether dose‑dependent improvements in RT could be observed and to assess the safety profile of the drug at different dosages. The results were summarized in Table 1 below, showing a clear trend of decreasing RT with increasing dose, while SD values remained relatively stable across groups.
stem: Which condition had the lowest mean reaction time?
explanation: The table shows the lowest mean RT (260 ms) for the High Dose group.
trap: Some may incorrectly assume the Medium Dose group had the lowest RT because it is the middle dose.

stem: Which factor was manipulated by the researchers to assess its effect on reaction time?
explanation: The study varied the dose of the cognitive enhancer (5 mg, 10 mg, 20 mg) while keeping other conditions constant.
trap: Participants might think age or task difficulty were manipulated because they are common variables in cognitive studies.

stem: What is the percent reduction in mean reaction time from Control to High Dose?
trap: Students may miscalculate using the wrong numerator or denominator, or round too early.

stem: Which condition had the highest standard deviation?
explanation: The Medium Dose group shows the highest SD (50 ms) among the four conditions.
trap: Because the SD values are close, some may mistakenly pick the Control or High Dose groups.

stem: Which statement about the dose-response pattern in Table 1 is best supported?

options.A: Mean RT was lower at each higher dose level than at the previous level.
options.B: Mean RT fell by the same number of ms per mg at every dose step.
options.C: The High Dose group had a smaller SD than the Control group.
options.D: The Low Dose group had a higher mean RT than the Control group.

explanation: Correct: A) Means fall 350, 320, 290, 260 ms across Control, Low, Medium, High. Why the others are wrong: B) The drop is 30 ms per step, but the steps span 5, 5 and 10 mg, so the fall is 6, 6 and 3 ms per mg. C) High Dose SD (47 ms) is larger than Control SD (45 ms). D) Low Dose (320 ms) is lower than Control (350 ms).
trap: Assuming equal 30 ms steps mean a constant effect per mg, when the last step covers 10 mg and the effect per mg is half as large.
